# OpenAI Dart Client

> Dart client for the OpenAI API with Responses API, Decisions API, Chat Completions, images, videos, audio, custom tools, embeddings, evals, realtime, signed webhooks, safety retrieval, structured monitoring errors, and more.

## Docs

- [HTTP/2 transport evaluation](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/specs/api-alignment/reviews/46-http2.md) (~3.1k tokens): Local TLS compatibility and matched benchmark evidence; defer experimental native adapter adoption, with no production transport change.

- [README](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/README.md) (~33.3k tokens): Primary package documentation with installation, configuration, and usage examples.
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/CHANGELOG.md) (~21.7k tokens): Release history and version-by-version changes.
- [MIGRATION](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/MIGRATION.md) (~22.2k tokens): Upgrade notes and breaking-change guidance.
- [Monitoring failures](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/README.md#how-do-i-inspect-monitoring-failures): Shared passive HTTP/failed Response/WS details, flat nullable SSE errors, scoped investigation and migration boundaries.

- [voice_consents_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/voice_consents_example.dart) (~1.2k tokens): Offline complete consent lifecycle, two explicit pages and browser MIME normalization; five default mock requests, six with explicit --delete, no API cost.

## Voice consent management

client.audio.voiceConsents is cached and supports create/list/retrieve/update/delete with abort, shared auth and conservative retries. Create is a three-field multipart upload with immutable recording bytes, filename and optional normalized MIME metadata; eight supported bases and 10 MiB limit. Update is required-name JSON POST. List only accepts after/limit and fetches one page; cursor presence distinguishes omission/null/value. Closed canonical responses preserve immutable receive-only future extras; deleted false remains false. Private default diagnostics/logs retain explicit caller error/HTTP context. Eligible project/access, api.voices.write and the current consent phrase are service requirements; recordings/sample must come from the same person/project. Sample-derived voice creation is available through client.audio.voices.create; no undocumented consent_phrases DTO is invented.

## Custom voice creation

- [voices_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/voices_example.dart) (~1.1k tokens): Offline explicit consent upload, sample-derived voice creation and custom reference JSON; two mock requests, $0 API cost.

client.audio.voices is cached; its create(CustomVoiceCreateRequest) method sends only multipart POST /audio/voices. Required name/audio_sample/consent; optional type is only audio_sample and stays omitted when unspecified. Names use 1–256 Unicode code points; original immutable sample bytes/filename, eight supported MIME bases, browser MIME normalization and 10 MiB limit share consent upload behavior without leaking name/type restrictions. CustomVoice validates fixed audio.voice/audio_sample, required id/name/integer created_at and immutable finite receive-only future extras; unknown known creation types are rejected. Use AudioVoice.custom(voice.id).toJson() as caller-selected reference without invoking speech/Live or widening another API's voice field. Approved same-person/project access and api.voices.write/read are service requirements; samples need five seconds of actual speech, 15 transcribed tokens and at most 30 seconds, without local quality/transcription validators. Shared auth/abort/errors/closed guards, no multipart replay, private automatic diagnostics/logging and original caller context. Creation only; no invented voice CRUD.

## File audio and Chat voices

ChatAudioConfig accepts typed open/custom AudioVoice references and marin/cedar; AAC is appended while pcm16 stays Chat-specific. File transcription already has all 14 form fields; fileContentType is optional file-part MIME metadata. Use gpt-transcribe with plural languages and supported keywords; specialist verbose/subtitle/diarization/English translation modes depend on the model. Translation create is JSON-only, createVerbose accepts canonical responses without task, and createRaw preserves text/SRT/VTT whitespace. Buffered file methods accept abortTrigger; transcription streams complete on valid transcript.text.done without replay. Received metadata/bytes/collections are immutable and private automatic diagnostics are redacted.

The February 26, 2027 Whisper/GPT-4o file-transcription sunset requires workflow-aware migration to gpt-transcribe/gpt-live-transcribe; retain operational specialist outputs until a replacement fits. It is separate from January 6 TTS and January 20 legacy snapshot notices. See README and MIGRATION for widened getters, appended enum cases and removed collection constructor const.

## Live HTTP sessions

- [live_http_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/live_http_example.dart) (~2.2k tokens): Offline caller-SDP WebRTC and SIP signaling, explicit refer/hangup, verified incoming notice with opt-in accept/reject, buffered/streamed stereo WAV and REST fork; seven default mock requests, $0 API cost.

client.live.sessions is cached and implements create/accept/reject/refer/hangup/fork/downloadRecording/downloadRecordingStream. Canonical create supports WebRTC offers and outbound SIP (E.164 destination, TLS provider URL, Digest auth, caller number), beyond the pinned clients' narrower helpers. SIP 201 means initialized before answer; ambiguous POST timeout/connection/5xx is sent once, and tracing does not deduplicate. Exact 201 JSON/empty 200/WAV response modes, shared auth/abort/errors, opaque encoded IDs and closed-client guards. Content has its own live_ ID pattern and preserves WAV plus 503 Retry-After. Storage defaults false, needs project policy, excludes ZDR; finalized recordings last 30 days. No polling or automatic call actions. Verify live.transport.incoming and use data.sessionId for an explicitly chosen control.

Complete shared startup/media/fork/session/audio/history/frontend/delegation models preserve declared fields, optional/null/absence, copy/clear and finite immutable open JSON. Thirteen distinct Live tool input variants plus nested shell helpers; 12 typed specific choices and allowed_tools 1–128. Service runtime support may be narrower than canonical wire coverage. Startup model/voice/history/audio format/instructions/delegation mode remain immutable; updates change backend settings. PCM16LE at 16/24 kHz and G.711 PCMA/PCMU at 8 kHz are primary-WebSocket formats; WebRTC/SIP omit audio.format. Live custom voice objects are open with IDs of 1–128 characters, independently of Speech's closed custom reference. Default logs/diagnostics redact private wire data; explicit caller models/errors remain readable. Primary/sideband/fork transports, codecs, compact Responses dispatch and transcript helpers are available; reconnect/queue/media conveniences remain inventoried.

Outbound SIP creation enforces the documented 1 MiB serialized UTF-8 body limit. The service limits ringing to three minutes and connected calls to two hours; request configuration does not change these durations. Forks reject known inherited model/voice/instructions/history overrides even through raw JSON, while preserving unrelated finite future metadata.

## Live WebSockets

- [live_websocket_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/live_websocket_example.dart) (~2.6k tokens): Offline primary/sideband conversations, concurrent observers, manual client delegation and two function outputs before one explicit continuation; synthetic peers, $0 API cost.

client.live.connect() opens an unstarted primary socket without a model query; start(LiveSessionStartEvent) waits session.started. client.live.attach(id, gracefulClose: ...) attaches without startup/audio submission. Typed primary/sideband writers admit 11/9 commands and all 22 received events, resolving narrower received aliases. LiveInputItem covers every declared canonical backend input branch separately from narrower ordinary Responses helpers. Response.event preserves arbitrary finite nested JSON, compact lifecycle snapshots and omission/null delegation IDs. Reflected sideband audio is original mono PCM16LE 24 kHz with output timestamps; keep delivery order/frame gaps. No Realtime commit, writable DTMF, implicit reconnect/replay or action runner.

closeSession installs final tracking before sending, blocks new work, drains with caller timeout/abort and confirms only LiveSessionClosed. close() is local transport cleanup; owned sockets close once and borrowed adapters retain ownership. latestUsageSeconds replaces cumulative audio snapshots; keep Responses backend tokens separate. Concurrent taps observe events without owning socket lifetime. Browser defaults reject every configured header before provider auth; use trusted signaling/caller WebRTC channels or explicitly injected proxy adapters. Wrap HTTP-started caller data channels with LivePrimaryConnection(adapter, sessionAlreadyStarted: true, ownsSocket: false), optionally with a known initialSession; duplicate startup/audio append are rejected. No Live ephemeral-key endpoint. Applications own authorization/execution, IDs, deduplication and all function results before one response.create; no item-create success ack.

## Stored Live forks and transcripts

- [live_workflows_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/live_workflows_example.dart) (~4.2k tokens): Offline finalized/stored originals, two mock WAV downloads, client/Responses forks, inherited voice/instructions/history, explicit app-state restoration, interleaved/canceled call IDs, captions and borrowed-channel cleanup; $0 API cost.

client.live.forkConnection(sourceId) opens the exact stored-session route with no model query or automatic startup. start(LiveForkSessionStartEvent(session: LiveForkSessionConfigParam())) explicitly inherits settings. New fork writers admit only documented root/audio overrides, excluding WebRTC permissions and inherited model/voice/instructions/history; old shared HTTP DTO open metadata is retained. Store requires project policy and non-ZDR; wait for session.closed and recording finalization. New WS format defaults PCM16 24k independently of source. No startup/audio/tool/action replay or automatic backend restoration.

LiveResponsesEvent.fromLiveEvent dispatches sparse lifecycle snapshots via LiveCompactResponse, reuses ordinary granular codecs where source contracts match, and preserves finite future or incompatible child shapes as raw views. Known malformed fields remain errors. The nested type is separate from required outer source.type response.event. Collect all active function calls through backend generation finalization before every output and one explicit continuation; empty compact output/tools is not a pending-call ledger. IDs/canceled outcomes/authorization/execution belong to one application action owner; backend/session/playback lifetimes remain separate.

LiveTranscriptGrouper attaches a non-consuming event tap; complete segment snapshots replace caption text by local ID. SDK grouping defaults are 500/2000/1000/2000 ms plus a 50 ms settle window, with event-ID dedup, timestamp reset, acknowledgments/interruptions and monotonic inactivity fallback. Raw taps remain lossless while grouping can suppress backchannels. Helper closure cancels only its timer/tap; finalized requires observed session.closed. Pure LiveTranscriptGrouping uses explicit source time. projectLiveTranscriptPlayback is an additive Dart caller-clock projection, not SDK hardware playback or audible completion. LiveConnection.dataChannel(callerChannel) is a typed already-started borrowed writer; cleanup never closes caller media/listeners. Opt-in reconnect/unsent queues/escape hatches/media engines remain inventory.

## Decisions image references

DecisionInputPart.image admits exact case-sensitive `data:`, `http://`, `https://` prefixes through constructors/parsers/copies. Strings are preserved, including escapes/query/fragment; the service checks image validity and public accessibility. The client does not fetch or normalize images. imageBytes and omitted detail/auto behavior remain compatible; all four ImageDetail values and 128-image request limit remain. File IDs/unsupported roles/audio/tools stay excluded. Current canonical schema and HTTP reference supersede older inline-only guide/SDK prose. The offline URL example closes its caller-owned mock transport.

## Safety alert explanations

SafetyAlert exposes typed detailedExplanation and hasDetailedExplanation, preserving absent/null/string including empty text. Constructor omission can adopt a valid explanation from legacy rawJson; explicit typed/presence inputs win. copyWith omission preserves, detailedExplanation:null retains a null key and hasDetailedExplanation:false removes it from effective JSON. Known raw values remain validated and cannot override typed values or resurrect cleared keys; finite future JSON is deeply immutable. rawJson retains the detached received snapshot, including an original explanation after effective clear; toJson reflects current typed presence/value. Equality/hash follow complete effective JSON and default diagnostics redact explanation/private metadata. The service determines temporary eligible-ZDR availability; reason:null does not prove eligibility. Existing explicit project GET/scoping remains, with no alert list/control/cache or changed webhook field. The Responses monitoring explanation remains optional nonnull. The offline example closes its caller-owned mock transport.

## Live files and published artifacts

- [agent_files_artifacts_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/agent_files_artifacts_example.dart) (~1.2k tokens): Offline input copy, distinct live opaque-page versus artifact-ID pagination, completed-turn metadata, exact bytes and byte-stream downloads after mocked environment expiry, artifact deletion and borrowed transport cleanup; $0 API cost.

client.agents.environments.files.create/list use existing file_id or standard-base64 inline configs directly. Live pages require object:page and nullable next; advance page with identical path/limit/order. client.agents.sessions.artifacts.list/retrieve/delete/download/downloadStream preserve immutable session/environment/turn ownership, original hosted path, size and publication timestamp. Artifact pages use after/lastId and nullable environment filter, with required nullable firstId/lastId. Null query values are omitted. All routes force agents=v1; byte downloads force octet-stream and remove Content-Type, preserve NUL/non-UTF8/empty bytes, use no JSON/text decoding or replay/interceptors, and borrow injected transports. Distinct factory transports are owned. Local abort/cancel releases only observation/download; no session action, delete or local filesystem path is chosen. Published completed-hosted-turn outputs survive environment expiry; unpublished outputs may not survive cancellation/deletion. Retain downloads before session deletion. Artifact deletion leaves live files intact. Canonical metadata sizes have no upper cap; guide file-reference/publication limits remain service-owned. Subagent inspection is available through the child resource; helpers retain deferred tracking.

## Child inspection and history

- [agent_subagents_example.dart](https://github.com/davidmigloz/ai_clients_dart/blob/main/packages/openai_dart/example/agent_subagents_example.dart) (~1.3k tokens): Offline six GET routes, typed inline child-list envelope, received closed/resumed state, separate root/child/turn history and ID pagination; nine mock requests, borrowed cleanup and $0 API cost.

client.agents.sessions.subagents.list/retrieve, .items.list, .turns.list/retrieve and .turns.items.list inspect service-owned child state. All six GETs force agents=v1 and retain normal auth/project/HTTP/abort policy with opaque nested IDs. ID lists use limit1–100/order/exclusive after, required nullable firstId/lastId and null-query omission. AgentSessionSubagentList is the exact inline list response, not a new canonical schema name. All 63 named closure contracts are reused unchanged, including all 17 history branches and full turn error/usage/timestamps. Child name/instructions/closedAt are required nullable; received instructions preserve output_text/encrypted_content and preview placeholders. OpenedAt remains stable on service resume while closedAt becomes null; reading does not create this transition. Root coordinator history differs from child and child-turn history. No child create/resume/interrupt/close endpoint, independent worker, permissions or automatic tool/history replay is added. Finite future values remain deeply owned, malformed known fields fail privately, and provider/connector/response-stream failures are guarded only at the six new GET origins while local HTTP/parse/timeout/abort classes retain their existing policy. Original causes remain explicit; diagnostic messages omit private payloads. Borrowed clients remain caller-owned. HTTP2 evaluation is the only remaining separate bounded work item after this core merge; helpers and later parity stay deferred.
